chapter: Buddy Petit and Sam Morgan years
title: Playing with Armstrong at Pete Lala's, then leaving for Los Angeles
summary: Williams played little with Louis Armstrong, who left for the boat; Williams played around until going to Los Angeles in 1919, narrowly missing the draft.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: A little, very few. I didn't play many. See, because I left, you see. I must play about one or two, because I left, you see. After we played Pete Lollars, after that 1916, you know, rave. Well, we went in Pete Lollars, you see, about 17 and the war started, come out, you know, broke out. Mm-hmm. And, uh, well, I didn't play, but he went on the boat, I think, or Tom Anderson's one of the two. I just remember now, see. Mm-hmm. Well, he broke up to the band he had, you see. He went to Tom Anderson on the boat. It was one of the other.
The way he went, I just remember now. So, uh, I played around with different fellas until, uh, 1919. And then I left and went to Los Angeles, and I mean, Manuel Manetta, and Wade Will and Mutt Carey.
They never did draft you, huh?

No. They had me gone, but they all broke up. I was to leave on the 12th, and I was on 11th. Oh, yeah. Wasn't that luck. Oh, yeah. Wasn't that luck. Yeah. And on the 12th of November, I was just ready to go.
